notes: The load/populate/unload order machine is exact: test_chunkload.c replays the oracle's ChunkLoadProbe recordings (out/java/chunkload) event for event, including addPlayer's radius square, updateMountedMovingPlayer's moved square and filterChunkLoadQueue's spiral. What is missing is the packet-facing half, which the GPU-path client does not consume. Closed by lane/idxworld: the packet side is ported onto the client world the client player collides with: serverreplay_sync_client is updatePlayerInstances' flush in the next world tick (the world tick's own writes of this tick, the entity pass's and the network tick's of the tick before; an explosion's with its S27), each cell as it stands at the flush. S23, S22 and S21 all carry the cells' final blocks and metadata, so the choice among them changes nothing the client world's blocks hold (an S21's sections also carry their light, and after an S22 or S23 the client relights itself; the native client world's light is read by nothing, since the player's collisions and the display ticks read blocks and the live renderer draws the server's world); the tile description packets are the S35 record's. The live renderer draws the server's own world rather than this client world (play.c's render world), so a server-driven block change shows in its frame at once, two ticks ahead of Java's client: a renderer follow-up, not this class.
